question: A pen is purchased for ₹40 and sold for ₹50. Find the profit percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Cost Price to Selling Price = 40 : 50 = 4 : 5

Profit = 5 − 4 = 1 part

Profit % = (Profit parts ÷ Cost Price parts) × 100

Profit % = (1 ÷ 4) × 100 = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 CP = ₹40
 
 
 SP = ₹50
 
 

 

 
 + ₹10 (Profit)

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) of the pen = ₹40

Selling Price (SP) of the pen = ₹50

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Profit = 50 − 40

⇒ Profit = ₹10

⇒ Profit % = (10 ÷ 40) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (1 ÷ 4) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

When Cost Price (CP) > Selling Price (SP), a loss is incurred. Loss = CP − SP. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount. Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Successive Discount

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are offered, the effective combined discount is given by the formula: [a + b − (a × b ÷ 100)]%.
